objective: Proof and exhaustive computation. (1) Blurring a law (each value replaced by a block of copies) keeps which systems fail and which variable sets are circuits, so it keeps cycle-like composition, and multiplies counts by block sizes. (2) Every Mal'tsev law on three values composes like cycles: a three-element Mal'tsev algebra has at most one nontrivial congruence (all 531441 Mal'tsev operations checked). (3) Blurred signed parity on three values (one value doubled) is Mal'tsev, composes like cycles, has knots and recognisable failures, and counts #P-complete (its count matrix has rank 2, so it is not strongly balanced): the formal bridge exists at three values. Of the 1020 non-simple Mal'tsev operations on three values, exactly the 48 with an affine quotient preserve it. (4) Blurred Z3 on four values does the same.
status: Proved by BEYOND-TWO-20261101-001B-P001: blurring a law (a value doubled) keeps its failing systems and circuits, so its cycle-like composition, and weights its counts by preimage sizes; every Mal'tsev law on three values composes like cycles (at most one nontrivial congruence; all 531441 operations checked); blurred signed parity on three values is Mal'tsev (the 48 non-simple operations with an affine quotient), has knots, fails recognisably and counts #P-complete (count matrix of rank 2): mutual selection in PINNING C's sense with cycle-like composition, so the exclusion is exactly two-valued; blurred signed Z3 on four values likewise
title: Blurring makes counts hard and keeps failures and composition
